theme: Data-hosting mirrors pointed at from GitHub: Zenodo, Figshare, Harvard Dataverse, HuggingFace, Kaggle, Mendeley Data collections on Airbnb, STR, hotels, tourism
queries_run: gh search repos "dataverse short term rental"
gh search repos "huggingface datasets hotel booking"
gh search repos "vacasa OR sonder dataset"
WebSearch site:github.com zenodo airbnb dataset repository (blocked, session budget exhausted)
WebSearch site:github.com huggingface.co/datasets airbnb OR hotel (blocked, session budget exhausted)
WebFetch raw READMEs for tomslee/airbnb-data-collection, rsanjabi/short-term-rentals-warehouse, derodz/ml-shorttermrentals, dolmios/airindex-2022
gh api repos/.../contents/ for rsanjabi/short-term-rentals-warehouse, muhammadyasin79/berlin-airbnb-tableau-dashboard, dagrewal/istanbul-airbnb-analysis

candidates.name: short-term-rentals-warehouse
candidates.what_it_holds: dbt-based data pipeline/warehouse claiming to extract Inside Airbnb listing data via http://insideairbnb.com/get-the-data.html plus Kaggle 'World Cities Population and Location' and Kaggle 'Cost of Living Indices' (Numbeo). README states coverage 2015-2020, 'over 35 million records'. Repo root has only .env.example, .gitignore, README.md and an empty dbt/ folder scaffold — no raw data files or seeds committed; extraction happens at runtime via src/extract.py (not inspected further). If the extractor actually reaches an Inside Airbnb archive going back to 2015, this is a lead on gap #1 (pre-2023 historical dumps), but this is unconfirmed from the README alone.
candidates.why_useful: If functional, would extend our Inside Airbnb panel (currently Dec 2022+) back to 2015, closing gap #1 (historical/archived Inside Airbnb dumps) and giving pre-COVID STR supply baselines.
candidates.last_activity: unknown (not in first search page metadata)
candidates.size_hint: claimed 35M+ records (not verified; not committed to repo)

candidates.name: berlin-airbnb-tableau-dashboard
candidates.what_it_holds: Tableau packaged workbook Berlin_Airbnb_Dashboard.twbx (6.68MB, contains an embedded data extract) plus a PNG dashboard image. Described as '14,274 Berlin Airbnb listings ... across 12 districts using real 2026 data'. Berlin is not in our 13-city Inside Airbnb panel.
candidates.why_useful: A committed, recent (2026) Berlin listings snapshot outside our current 13-city panel; Berlin STR data also matters for the regulation gap (#12, Berlin has active STR registration rules). Extraction requires Tableau or a .twbx unpacker (it's a zip of a data extract + XML), not a plain CSV.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Overlaps in kind with our existing Inside Airbnb panel but different city (Berlin not held)

candidates.name: istanbul-airbnb-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Analysis of Istanbul Airbnb accommodation 'using data from www.insideairbnb.com'; repo has a Code/ folder and (per truncated listing) likely a Data folder not fully inspected. Istanbul is outside our 13-city Inside Airbnb panel and outside APAC/EMEA coverage we hold.
candidates.why_useful: Potential Istanbul-market Inside Airbnb snapshot; Turkey/Istanbul tourism is a data-thin region for us (adjacent to APAC/EMEA gap #7). Not fully verified whether raw data files are actually committed vs. just referenced.

candidates.name: airbnb-data-collection
candidates.what_it_holds: Original (pre-Inside-Airbnb) Airbnb listing scraper by Tom Slee, storing results in a PostgreSQL schema (postgresql/schema_current.sql) with tables for rooms, surveys, search areas, neighborhoods. Actively used circa 2014-2019, since unmaintained per the author. No data files or archives are included in the repo itself — it is a tool, not a dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Historically this scraper generated some of the earliest publicly-shared Airbnb listing snapshots (predating Inside Airbnb, some cities back to ~2014-2015); forks or users of this tool sometimes published resulting CSVs elsewhere (Kaggle/Zenodo) — worth a targeted follow-up search for 'airbnb-data-collection' output dumps. As a live method it scrapes airbnb.com directly, which per our rules is a ToS decision for a human, not to be run.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Predates and is superseded by Inside Airbnb, which we already hold; only relevant if a data dump derived from it surfaces

candidates.name: ml-shorttermrentals
candidates.what_it_holds: ML notebook predicting daily STR rental rates using downloads from AllTheRooms.com (a subscription STR data vendor named explicitly in gap #2). Source CSVs are NOT committed ('I did not upload the source data' due to AllTheRooms redistribution restrictions); only a trained pickle model and notebook are present. Scope is a single zip code chosen by the author.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms AllTheRooms.com as a named, real vendor for realized STR rates (relevant to gap #2), and shows what fields/approach a downloaded AllTheRooms export contains, even though no data is redistributable here.

candidates.name: airindex-2022
candidates.what_it_holds: Landing page/project 'AirIndex' described as testing techniques for aggregating and providing open short-term rental data from Airbnb (project site referenced, not the repo itself). README does not detail specific fields, and no data files are evident; appears to be a marketing/landing-page repo (Next.js tooling, sitemap generation) rather than a working data pipeline.
candidates.why_useful: Concept is on-theme (an open Airbnb data aggregation index) but content/status could not be confirmed as functional or as holding real data; flagging in case the live site (airindex site referenced in repo) has since published something.

candidates.name: airdna-chatbot
candidates.what_it_holds: FastAPI + Next.js chatbot for querying AirDNA data (AirDNA is a paid STR analytics vendor named in gap #2). No data files committed; presumably calls AirDNA's paid API at runtime, which would require a paid key we are not allowed to use.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal — confirms AirDNA as an API-backed vendor but offers no free/committed data and needs a paid key, so not directly actionable under 'never use paid API keys'.

notes: This theme (Zenodo/Figshare/Dataverse/HuggingFace/Kaggle/Mendeley mirrors linked from GitHub) came up almost entirely empty on GitHub's repo-metadata text search: `gh search repos` matches only repo name/description/README-first-lines, not full README bodies or badge links to zenodo.org/DOI badges, so a repo that only has a 'DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.xxxx' badge deep in its README is invisible to this search. None of 'zenodo airbnb dataset', 'huggingface airbnb dataset', 'dataverse short term rental', 'zenodo tourism', 'mendeley data hotel', 'zenodo short-term rental', 'huggingface datasets hotel booking', 'figshare tourism dataset', 'harvard dataverse airbnb', 'hotel dataset huggingface', 'reddit airbnb dataset', 'wikipedia pageviews airbnb', or 'similarweb dataset github' returned any hits at all (empty arrays). Topic search (--topic=airbnb-dataset, --topic=short-term-rental, --topic=insideairbnb, --topic=tourism-dataset) surfaced mostly boilerplate NYC/Berlin/Istanbul EDA notebooks and SaaS/MCP-server products for STR property management (Kamra-PMS, RentTools.io, various Hospitable/Guesty/Channex MCP servers) which were excluded as non-data software products, not datasets. 'kaggle airbnb dataset' and 'AirDNA data'/'vacasa OR sonder dataset' returned only single-Kaggle-NYC-file tutorials or subscription-vendor wrappers, excluded per instructions. WebSearch was unavailable for the entire session (shared 200-call budget already exhausted by other concurrent scouts before I could use it), and WebFetch against github.com/search was rate-limited (HTTP 429, Retry-After 3600s) after two attempts — likely also from concurrent scout load on the same GitHub web endpoint. I substituted gh api contents/ listings (used 3 of the 8-call budget) and WebFetch of raw.githubusercontent.com README files (which was not rate-limited) to verify the most promising leads. Recommendation for a future pass on this exact theme: (a) retry the WebSearch-based site:zenodo.org / site:huggingface.co/datasets / site:dataverse.harvard.edu queries directly (not site:github.com) once budget resets, since a Zenodo/HF/Dataverse record page itself often links back to a GitHub repo in its 'Related identifiers' field, which is the reverse direction from what gh search text-matching can find; (b) try `gh search code "zenodo.org/record" airbnb` (one-shot, since code search is capped at 10/min) to find repos with a Zenodo badge/link buried in README body text that repo-search cannot see; (c) check huggingface.co/datasets directly for 'airbnb', 'hotel-booking', 'short-term-rental' tags via its own search UI (not a GitHub tool, but many HF dataset cards embed a GitHub companion-repo link).
